Tejaswini Hebalkar, SVP at Allstate Insurance Company, takes us through her journey in tech, shares lessons on leadership and explains why empathy will matter more in an AI-driven world.
Mirae Asset’s MAVI raises Rs 1,125 Cr in first close of Venture Opportunity Fund II
Mirae Asset Venture Investments (MAVI), the venture capital investment platform of the Mirae Asset Financial Group in India, has raised Rs 1,125 crore as the first close of its Rs 1,800 crore Mirae Asset Venture Opportunity Fund – II (MAVOF II/Fund).
Bluehill.VC raises Rs 400 Cr for maiden frontier-tech fund
Bluehill.VC, a frontier-tech-focused venture capital firm based in Chennai, announced the final close of its maiden Rs 400 crore fund, including the full subscription of its Rs 50 crore greenshoe option.
Funding news
Scrubsy raises Rs 27 Cr in seed funding
D2C home cleaning brand Scrubsy has raised Rs 27 crore in a seed funding round led by V3 Ventures. The company, operated by BoldChem Science Pvt Ltd, plans to use the capital to expand into new categories, including car cleaners, laundry care and other all-purpose home cleaning solutions. Scrubsy aims to become India’s first digital-native brand to lead the home cleaning category at scale.
The company says it has grown 100% year-on-year and acquired more than 5 lakh customers within eight months of launch. It is targeting Rs 100 crore in annual recurring revenue by FY28. Scrubsy has been bootstrapped and EBITDA-positive since inception, it says. Its product portfolio includes kitchen, bathroom and shoe cleaning solutions focused on performance and convenience.
Invisel raises Rs 4 Cr led by IAN Angel Fund
Nanotechnology-based home surface protection brand Invisel has raised Rs 4 crore in funding led by IAN Angel Fund, with participation from BeyondSeed and FAAD Capital. The round marks the company’s first external funding after building a profitable business through bootstrapping. Invisel will use the capital to establish a dedicated manufacturing and research facility in Pune, strengthen materials science capabilities, accelerate product innovation and expand in domestic and international markets.
Founded by Atharva Ulangwar and Sumedh Yeolekar, Invisel develops protective coatings designed to prevent stains, hard water marks and everyday surface wear. Within over a year of commercial operations, the company has served more than 60,000 customers across 900-plus pin codes, generated Rs 5.2 crore in FY26 revenue and remained profitable.
Brilliance Cosmocare raises $200,000 seed funding
Mumbai-based skin health venture Brilliance Cosmocare has raised $200,000 in seed funding from a group of family offices and institutional investors. Founded by aesthetic surgeon Dr Ashok Patel, the company plans to use the capital to develop clinical infrastructure, expand its preventive-care product pipeline and strengthen its skin record data platform.
Brilliance positions itself around skin and hair longevity rather than conventional dermatology. Its approach begins with an AI-assisted diagnostic scan that evaluates factors including skin age, hydration, pigmentation, UV damage and barrier health. The resulting report is used by doctors to develop treatment plans. The company says its data-led approach is aimed at addressing gaps in the skincare and aesthetic medicine market.
Other news
Lightrock partially exits Kauvery Hospitals
Global investment platform Lightrock has announced a partial realisation of its investment in Kauvery Hospitals through Lightrock Growth Fund I. As part of the transaction, Lightrock will sell a portion of its stake to Kauvery’s promoters while retaining a meaningful ownership position and continuing to support the healthcare group’s growth.
Lightrock invested in Kauvery in August 2019 and has since worked with the hospital chain on expanding its footprint, strengthening clinical capabilities and improving access to healthcare across South India. The investment firm has also supported Kauvery through board representation. Established in 1999, Kauvery Hospitals began with a 30-bed facility in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu. It now operates 13 facilities with more than 2,500 beds and over 12,000 employees across six cities in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
IISc researchers launch multilingual speech model SraVaani
Researchers at IISc’s SPIRE Lab, in collaboration with ARTPARK and with support from Google, have released SraVaani, a multilingual Indian speech recognition model trained on 65 languages and dialects. The model includes more than 40 languages that are not officially supported by existing speech recognition systems.
SraVaani covers 20 scheduled languages and 45 regional languages and dialects, potentially expanding speech AI access to around 25 crore people whose languages are underserved. Its coverage spans regions across India and includes languages such as Garo, Angika, Chakma, Kokborok, Tulu, Bundeli and Bajjika. The model is publicly available on Hugging Face under an MIT licence, along with a demo and fine-tuning code. It is aimed at advancing low-resource speech-to-text, language detection and sovereign AI applications.
Capitalmind Mutual Fund reaches Rs 600 Cr AUM
Capitalmind Asset Management, the AMC of Capitalmind Mutual Fund, has completed one year since units of its first scheme, Capitalmind Flexi Cap Fund, were allotted on August 4, 2025. As of July 31, 2026, the fund house managed Rs 600 crore across four schemes for more than 13,000 investors. Investors were spread across 1,300 cities and towns, with 36% of individual investors coming from locations beyond the top 30 geographical markets identified by AMFI. Direct plans accounted for 84% of assets under management.
During its first year, Capitalmind expanded from one scheme to four and developed transaction and servicing access across direct, platform and distributor channels. The four schemes follow different investment approaches and portfolio requirements while sharing a focus on evidence-based decision-making, clear processes and disciplined execution.
HCLTech, NetApp expand hybrid cloud collaboration
HCLTech has expanded its collaboration with NetApp to offer hybrid cloud storage-as-a-service aimed at helping enterprises scale AI and data-driven workloads. The solution combines HCLTech’s Utility for Everything digital infrastructure framework with NetApp Keystone, a pay-as-you-go storage service. The consumption-based model allows organisations to scale storage, performance and data services according to changing workload requirements. It is designed to support AI and generative AI applications alongside traditional enterprise systems.
The offering also integrates with HCLTech’s AI Factory suite to support AI development, deployment and operations. By combining consumption-led infrastructure with NetApp’s data management capabilities, the companies aim to help enterprises move from AI pilots to larger-scale adoption. The solution also focuses on data readiness, governance and improving efficiency by running workloads closer to where data resides.
Deloitte India, CrowdStrike deepen cybersecurity partnership
Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu India LLP has expanded its strategic global partnership with CrowdStrike to help Indian organisations consolidate cybersecurity and strengthen security operations. The collaboration will provide wider access to CrowdStrike’s AI-native Falcon platform along with Deloitte India’s managed security services. The offering is designed to provide AI-powered protection, automated security operations and improved threat detection and response.
Deloitte India will help customers consolidate security capabilities on a single platform, enabling greater cross-domain visibility while reducing the cost and complexity associated with managing multiple security tools. The partnership will also provide consulting, transformation and managed security services to support Falcon deployments within existing technology environments. The companies said the expanded collaboration will help organisations strengthen their security posture as enterprises face increasing cybersecurity challenges in an AI-driven business environment.
BikeWo, Hala Mobility plan 1,000-EV fleet
BikeWo Green Tech has signed a memorandum of understanding with Hala Mobility to explore the deployment and management of electric vehicle fleets. The proposed first phase involves approximately 1,000 electric vehicles, with a strategic objective of scaling the deployment to around 10,000 vehicles over the next three years. The collaboration combines BikeWo’s capabilities in electric mobility and fleet operations with Hala Mobility’s participation in the mobility ecosystem.
During the initial phase, the companies will develop frameworks covering EV deployment, fleet utilisation, vehicle management and related operational requirements. Performance from the first phase will be assessed to determine the pace and scope of further expansion. The partnership aims to establish a scalable EV fleet operating model based on operational performance, commercial viability and evolving market requirements.
Salesforce, Tripura government target 10,000 digital learners
Salesforce and the Directorate of Information Technology, Government of Tripura, have announced a collaboration to expand digital skills and workforce readiness across the state. Announced at the Destination Tripura Business Conclave 2026 in Agartala, the initiative will use Salesforce’s Trailhead online learning platform to prepare students, youth, government employees and entrepreneurs for an AI-driven economy.
The programme aims to reach more than 10,000 learners by 2027. Participants will have access to self-paced learning paths covering CRM, business analysis, technology fundamentals and other areas. Salesforce will also provide orientation resources and support for learners using the platform. The Directorate of Information Technology will identify participants through government departments, educational institutions and skill-development agencies, while supporting awareness and wider access to the programme across Tripura.
Uber expands services to 100 more Indian cities
Uber has expanded into 100 additional Indian cities, taking its footprint to 225 cities across the country. The expansion will initially be powered by Uber Bike, offering affordable mobility options in smaller towns while creating flexible earning opportunities for local drivers. The new operations will span 18 states and one union territory. Uber Bike is intended to support short-distance travel, first- and last-mile connectivity and journeys through congested urban areas.
The company said two-wheelers are playing an increasingly important role in India’s everyday mobility. For riders, the service provides an affordable travel option, while drivers can access flexible earning opportunities using vehicles they already own. The expansion represents one of Uber’s largest moves in India and significantly broadens its presence beyond major urban centres.
Plugzmart to invest Rs 100 Cr in Tamil Nadu
Tamil Nadu-based EV charging technology company Plugzmart has signed an MoU with the Government of Tamil Nadu to invest Rs 100 crore in expanding its manufacturing footprint, research and development capabilities and charging infrastructure ecosystem. The investment is expected to generate more than 500 direct high-skilled jobs over the next three years across hardware engineering, power electronics, embedded software and advanced manufacturing.
Incubated at IIT Madras Research Park, Plugzmart operates as a full-stack EV infrastructure company. It designs and manufactures AC and DC fast chargers ranging from 3.3 kW to 360 kW, along with ARAI-compliant charger controllers, Power Line Communication modules and cloud-native Charger Management Systems. The investment will increase production capacity at its manufacturing facility in Oragadam and Vallam, strengthening Tamil Nadu’s EV infrastructure ecosystem.
Mahindra University launches open-source HackerFab
Mahindra University has launched India’s second HackerFab, following the student-led facility at IIT Bombay, and the country’s first university-sponsored, student-led open-source semiconductor fabrication facility. The initiative is aimed at strengthening India’s semiconductor capabilities and supporting the Atmanirbhar Bharat vision. The facility will enable students to design and develop low-cost fabrication tools for education and research, providing practical exposure to semiconductor manufacturing. Led by students from the university’s B.Tech. programme in VLSI Design & Technology, the HackerFab will focus on developing core semiconductor fabrication equipment.
T-Hub launches 12-month deeptech founder fellowship
T-Hub has launched Blueprint, a 12-month founder fellowship designed to support deeptech startups moving from early traction to scale. The programme was announced as part of HYD – Deep Tech: Next, a founder-focused initiative that brought entrepreneurs into discussions with the Technology Development Board of the Department of Science and Technology. Under Blueprint, T-Hub will work with deeptech founders as a generalist CXO, helping build operating and commercial foundations required for growth.
Founders will receive a 12-month operating plan, support to prepare for fundraising, a VC-ready pitch and a complete data room covering financials, ownership, legal documentation and business traction. T-Hub will also facilitate investor interactions, enterprise contracts and international exposure, alongside one-to-one mentorship, talent pipelines and access to market-oriented intellectual property.
CapitalXB deploys Biz2X digital lending platform
CapitalXB Finance, an RBI-regulated NBFC-Factor focused on supply-chain, working-capital and trade finance, has implemented an end-to-end digital lending and supply-chain finance platform powered by Biz2X. The technology deployment forms part of CapitalXB’s strategy to build a technology-led trade-finance platform combining digital credit, regulated lending, export finance, foreign exchange, compliance and distribution.
Through the Biz2X platform, CapitalXB has reduced KYC and client onboarding timelines from two to three days to less than an hour. AI-assisted credit assessment has also improved credit turnaround times by more than 80%. Over the next 12 to 18 months, the partnership is expected to support more than 250 SMEs and MSMEs and facilitate over Rs 1,000 crore in disbursements. The platform will also help CapitalXB scale transaction volumes and expand financing products and trade corridors.
AscentHR appoints Shivaprasad Mundakana as CHRO
HR technology and workforce solutions company AscentHR has appointed Shivaprasad Mundakana as its Chief Human Resources Officer, effective July 1, 2026. He joins the leadership team as the company expands across India and international markets.
In his new role, Mundakana will lead AscentHR’s people strategy, focusing on leadership development and organisational readiness for the company’s M&A-led expansion. He will oversee HR integration for acquired businesses and develop scalable people processes across geographies. His responsibilities will also include strengthening employee engagement and aligning employee and client success as AscentHR expands across APAC, the Middle East, ANZ and Africa.
Autodesk elevates Nikhil Bagalkotkar to lead AEC business
Autodesk has elevated Nikhil Bagalkotkar as Head – Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC), India and SAARC, effective immediately. In the new role, Bagalkotkar will lead the company’s AEC business strategy across the region and drive adoption of Autodesk’s Design and Make platform. He will focus on expanding the AEC business, strengthening customer and partner engagement and accelerating digital workflows across the design, engineering and construction lifecycle. Bagalkotkar brings nearly 20 years of technology and business leadership experience and has been with Autodesk for seven years.
Sujeeth Pai to become SKF India Industrial MD
SKF India (Industrial) has announced the appointment of Sujeeth Pai as its Managing Director, effective September 1, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. Pai will lead the company’s operations and drive its profitable growth agenda. He will succeed Mukund Vasudevan, who will become President for the Industrial Region covering India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Vasudevan will transition to the role of Non-Executive Director on the board.
Aurionpro wins Rs 100 Cr AI data centre order
Data centre solutions provider Aurionpro Solutions has secured an order valued at nearly Rs 100 crore from a global hyperscale data centre operator. The order involves building and project-managing digital infrastructure for the customer’s upcoming AI-ready data centre in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra. The latest contract expands Aurionpro’s existing partnership with the hyperscaler and reflects continued confidence in the company’s technology capabilities and project execution expertise. The order strengthens Aurionpro’s position in the rapidly expanding data centre market, particularly in AI-ready infrastructure.
Bubble Me rebrands as magnesium-first wellness brand
Indian wellness brand Bubble Me has rebranded as it evolves from a bath and body care company into a magnesium-first wellness brand. The new identity reflects the company’s expanding product portfolio and focus on making everyday wellness more accessible, simple and science-backed. Founded around the belief that self-care should be enjoyable and approachable, Bubble Me has expanded over the past two years based on consumer insights and product innovation. Its focus now includes wellness needs such as recovery, sleep, stress management and targeted comfort.
Leah selects Oracle Cloud for global expansion
Leah, an agentic operating system for enterprise commercial work, has selected Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to support the global expansion of its Leah Agentic OS platform. The platform autonomously manages legal, contracting, procurement and finance workflows, while its Maestro super orchestrator coordinates agents, workflows and automation across enterprise systems. Leah expects OCI to improve platform performance by up to 30% and reduce cloud operating costs by up to 40%. Founded in 2015, Leah serves more than 400 enterprise customers.
Visafir waives visa service fees for select applicants
Technology-led visa facilitation company Visafir has announced an Independence Day initiative under which it will waive its visa facilitation service fee for girls below 18 years, senior citizens aged 60 and above, and retired armed forces personnel until August 31, 2026. Eligible applicants will receive assistance with visa documentation and application preparation without paying Visafir’s service fee. However, embassy charges applicable to the destination will continue to be borne by applicants. The company’s support includes organising documents, understanding destination-specific requirements and preparing applications for submission. Visafir combines AI-powered documentation with expert human verification, providing applicants with structured assistance while retaining human oversight at key stages.

articles.title: Qualcomm Introduces $300 Laptops With Snapdragon C, Outruns Intel N250 by Up to 67%
articles.text:
Thursday, August 13th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Qualcomm Introduces $300 Laptops With Snapdragon C, Outruns Intel N250 by Up to 67%
Qualcomm is finally unveiling the specifications of its entry-level, low-cost Snapdragon C platform. According to the specifications, the platform features up to eight Arm cores for systems expected to start around the $300 mark. In a market where DRAM and NAND Flash are extremely expensive, Qualcomm aims to give students, families, and basic office workers a modern laptop at a low price of just $300. Snapdragon C uses Qualcomm's Kryo CPU architecture, with frequencies reaching up to 3.0 GHz for single-core workloads and 2.0 GHz for multicore scenarios. The chip also includes 2 MB of cache, an integrated Adreno A643 GPU clocked at up to 900 MHz, and surprisingly a Hexagon NPU for lighter AI workloads. Qualcomm supports up to 16 GB of LPDDR4x, LPDDR5, or LPDDR5x memory, along with PCIe 3.0 NVMe storage, UFS 2.2/3.1, and a wide range of connectivity options. Interestingly, LPDDR4x memory might be less expensive compared to the others, which could make a $300 laptop dream feasible.
The company is comparing Snapdragon C against Intel's N250 "Twin Lake" platform and claims significant performance advantages while running on battery. Depending on the workload, Qualcomm reports gains ranging from 24% to 67%, with Cinebench showing the largest differences at 50% faster single-threaded performance and up to 67% better multithreaded performance. Geekbench and Speedometer, which may better represent everyday laptop usage, are also claimed to favor Snapdragon C. Qualcomm's figures also indicate substantially better efficiency, including 106% higher efficiency during Netflix playback, 68% during web browsing, and 74% during Teams video calls. The company promotes this chip for all-day battery life, although real-world runtime will heavily depend on the configuration chosen by each manufacturer.The Snapdragon C platform will soon appear in laptops from Acer, ASUS, HP, and Lenovo, giving Qualcomm a chance to carve out a niche in the budget Windows-on-Arm segment. With budget section adopting Qualcomm's WoA designs, they will naturally transition to more powerful Snapdragon X2 Plus and X2 Elite designs. The $300 target will be particularly interesting given rising memory and component costs, which have made cheaper laptops harder to produce. On paper, Snapdragon C could offer a compelling combination of responsiveness, low power consumption, and modern connectivity at the lower end of the market. Whether Qualcomm's performance and efficiency claims translate into a genuinely better $300 laptop will ultimately depend on actual retail pricing, and what memory/storage configurations come at that price point.

And as for performance, what a massive feat that with 8 Kryo cores, it manages to beat Intel's 4 Efficient cores—and only when laptops are running on battery, no less. Why doesn't Qualcomm tell us how its chip performs against the N250 when laptops are plugged in? Because things probably aren't so favorable there.
Practically speaking, in my opinion, we're talking about a laptop with performance from ten years ago, albeit with great battery life. Perhaps a suitable choice for those who don't want—or never got used to—tablets. But that's as far as it goes.

articles.title: This modder shrunk a Steam Deck down to Game Boy size
articles.text:
In a nutshell: A Steam Deck mod built inside a Game Boy-sized case is nearing a key milestone: adding its internal display. The project, called SteamBoy, already has a working Steam Deck motherboard, battery, speakers and controls inside a custom case modeled after Nintendo's original handheld. However, the SteamBoy is still a work in progress, with the display remaining the largest unfinished component.
Fitting the AMOLED panel, completing the adapter board and applying the BIOS modification will determine whether the device can function as a self-contained handheld.
As the next step, creator PhyFawkes plans to install a 1,200 x 1,080 AMOLED panel with a 90 Hz refresh rate. The panel was originally designed for VR use, so it cannot connect directly to the Steam Deck's hardware. A custom adapter PCB is being designed to connect the Deck's display ribbon cable to the new screen.
The mod will also require a BIOS modification. PhyFawkes said the firmware work will be similar to modifications used in the DeckHD and Deck Sight projects. Until the display is installed and working, the SteamBoy can only be used with an external monitor.
"Hopefully it won't be too long before that's working as well," PhyFawkes wrote in a comment on a video showing the device running.
The build started with a simple question about the Steam Deck's internals. "The Steam Deck motherboard seems pretty small," PhyFawkes wrote. "I wonder if you could make a Steam Deck the size of a Game Boy?"
The project shows that much of the hardware can fit inside a much smaller enclosure. "It has a fully functional LCD Steam Deck motherboard, battery, speakers, and all the face buttons you see here. No custom PCBs needed (so far), and all within the dimensions of a Game Boy," PhyFawkes said.
That is the main technical point of the build. The modder has not needed to replace the Deck's main hardware or create custom control boards to make the system work in the smaller case. The display is the first component that requires a purpose-built circuit board.
SteamBoy Teardown and Assembly
by u/PhyFawkes in SteamDeckModded
Cooling is another challenge in the tightly packed enclosure. PhyFawkes used a 30 x 7 mm fan and heatsink from AliExpress, mounted with a custom 3D-printed bracket. The system also uses a slight undervolt to reduce heat. During gaming, temperatures have reportedly ranged from 70 to 80 degrees Celsius.
Teardown photos posted on Reddit show the Steam Deck components arranged inside the Game Boy-style shell. The design retains the general shape and control layout of the original handheld, but the system inside is built around Valve's modern portable PC hardware.
For now, the project demonstrates that a functional Steam Deck can be reduced to a much smaller, retro-style form factor without modifying its core motherboard, battery, speakers or controls.

articles.title: La configuración secreta de WhatsApp que libera hasta 10 GB de espacio en el teléfono
articles.text:
El almacenamiento insuficiente es uno de los problemas más habituales en los smartphones actuales. WhatsApp, una de las aplicaciones más utilizadas en el mundo, puede llegar a ocupar espacio vital en el teléfono debido a la acumulación de fotos, videos, audios y documentos.
Esta situación ralentiza el dispositivo y afecta la experiencia de uso. Conocer y activar la configuración adecuada puede liberar espacio de forma inmediata y mantener el móvil en óptimas condiciones.
PUBLICIDAD
El auge del intercambio de archivos multimedia y la tendencia a reenviar mensajes hacen que cada día se acumulen más datos en la memoria interna. La buena noticia es que la propia aplicación ofrece herramientas poco conocidas que permiten gestionar y eliminar elementos innecesarios en pocos pasos.
Cómo ver y gestionar el almacenamiento de WhatsApp
WhatsApp dispone de un panel específico para administrar el espacio que utiliza en el dispositivo. Para acceder:
- Dirígete a la pestaña de Chats y toca el ícono de menú.
- Selecciona Ajustes > Almacenamiento y datos > Administrar almacenamiento.
En la parte superior de la pantalla, se indica el espacio total que WhatsApp ocupa en el teléfono. Esta función permite identificar los archivos más pesados y organizarlos por tamaño o antigüedad.
PUBLICIDAD
Elimina archivos grandes y elementos reenviados muchas veces
Uno de los atajos más efectivos es revisar los elementos que han sido reenviados en múltiples ocasiones o que ocupan mucho espacio:
- En Administrar almacenamiento, verás sugerencias de limpieza, como “archivos grandes” o “elementos reenviados muchas veces”.
- Selecciona los archivos que deseas eliminar. Puedes mantener presionado para seleccionar varios o pulsar “Seleccionar todos” para una limpieza masiva.
- Confirma la eliminación. WhatsApp borrará definitivamente esos archivos de la aplicación.
Borra el contenido de chats individuales o grupales
Cada chat almacena su propio historial de archivos multimedia. Para liberar espacio de un chat específico:
- Abre el chat.
- Toca el nombre del contacto o grupo y selecciona Administrar almacenamiento.
- Visualiza el peso de las fotos, videos, documentos y audios asociados a esa conversación.
- Selecciona y elimina los elementos no deseados. Puedes filtrar por tipo de archivo o por tamaño.
Esta acción libera espacio sin eliminar todo el chat ni salir del grupo.
Cómo eliminar copias duplicadas y liberar aún más espacio
Con frecuencia, WhatsApp almacena varias copias de un mismo archivo en distintos chats o carpetas. Para erradicar duplicados:
- Ve a Ajustes > Almacenamiento y datos > Administrar almacenamiento.
- Marca la opción “Eliminar todas las copias” al seleccionar archivos para suprimir duplicados y evitar que ocupen espacio innecesario.
Usa la búsqueda avanzada para eliminar archivos individuales
La función de búsqueda avanzada permite localizar archivos específicos por tipo:
- Pulsa el campo de búsqueda en la parte superior de la lista de chats.
- Filtra por Fotos, Videos o Documentos.
- Elimina de forma selectiva los archivos que no necesitas.
Esta herramienta resulta ideal para limpiar elementos concretos sin revisar manualmente cada conversación.
Vacía el contenido multimedia de los chats sin perder mensajes importantes
WhatsApp permite vaciar el contenido multimedia de un chat conservando los mensajes de texto:
- Abre el chat, ve a Más > Vaciar chat.
- Elige si deseas borrar videos, fotos, stickers, documentos o audios.
- Marca o desmarca elementos según tu preferencia y confirma la limpieza.
Así, puedes mantener el historial de conversación y liberar espacio solo eliminando archivos pesados.
Recomendaciones y precauciones antes de borrar archivos
Antes de eliminar archivos, es recomendable hacer una copia de seguridad en Google Drive o iCloud. Esto asegura que no se pierdan fotos, videos o documentos importantes. Recuerda que al eliminar un archivo desde WhatsApp, este solo se borra para ti, no para los demás participantes del chat.
PUBLICIDAD
La gestión eficiente del almacenamiento en WhatsApp evita bloqueos, ralentizaciones y problemas de funcionamiento en el teléfono. Con unos minutos de revisión periódica, es posible liberar varios gigabytes de espacio y prolongar la vida útil del dispositivo.
Adoptar este hábito no solo mejora el rendimiento del móvil, también permite aprovechar nuevas funciones y actualizaciones sin preocuparse por el espacio disponible.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: If Apple sends you a push notification alerting you to a spyware attack, take it seriously | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple has sent out a new batch of notifications to customers who it suspects have been targeted with spyware capable of hacking into their devices. The tech giant sends out these notifications on occasion to alert its customers that their iPhones, iPads, or Macs might have been compromised with spyware typically used by governments.
Apple told TechCrunch that it sent out the notifications on Thursday to users targeted in 110 countries. Apple says to date it has notified customers in over 150 countries, giving some context to how far government-used spyware has spread around the world.
In a new support article on its website, Apple says it will notify users directly on their iPhone lock screen with a push notification that urges the person to take action. Apple told TechCrunch that it has updated the user experience, making it easier for recipients to access important information on what to do next.
When received, a threat notification will read: “Apple detected a mercenary spyware attack targeted at your iPhone. There are actions you can take now to protect your data and device.”
Apple also sends notifications by email and to users when they log in to their account.
John Scott-Railton, a senior researcher at digital research group Citizen Lab, first highlighted the latest batch of spyware notifications in a thread on X.
If you receive a notification like this, take it seriously. We’ve explained before what happens when someone gets a notification saying they’ve been targeted. It may not mean that you have been successfully hacked, but you should still take immediate steps to protect your device and data.
The push notification also opens up advice on who to reach out to for help. You will also be advised to switch on Lockdown Mode, a security feature that makes it far more difficult for spyware attacks to succeed. According to Apple, it has yet to see a case where someone’s device was hacked while Lockdown Mode was enabled.
Spyware attacks are generally rare, but the proliferation of the surveillance technology in recent years has allowed them to be abused by governments and deployed against critics, including members of civil society.
Citizen Lab’s Scott-Railton told TechCrunch that these new push notifications are a “big improvement” in urging people to seek help to secure their devices since Apple debuted its spyware alerts in 2021.
“Notifications create a critical signal that a community is being targeted. People get an alert, and then some of them reach out and seek help. Often this kicks off an investigation that reveals many, many more cases,” said Scott-Railton.
Citing the ongoing scandal in Poland over the former government’s use of spyware against its rivals, Scott-Railton said that without Apple’s notifications, “that entire massive scandal about spyware abuse in the Polish election wouldn’t have been uncovered.”

articles.title: Canadian pediatricians warn of rising e-scooter injuries, deaths among kids
articles.text:
Electric scooters, often called e-scooters, are a popular form of micromobility transport. They’re also surprisingly dangerous.
From battery-related fires to a sharp increase in injuries, e-scooters are taking a toll on Canadians. We wrote about the alarming number of battery fires in Toronto earlier this week, but a new report from CBC News calls attention to e-scooter injuries, particularly involving children.
SickKids’ pediatric emergency physician Dr. Daniel Rosenfield told CBC News he’s seen an “exponential rise” in injuries from e-scooter crashes. Putting it into numbers, SickKids saw 26 e-scooter injury cases in 2023, climbing to 46 in 2024 and then 107 in 2025. Rosenfield says the hospital is likely going to surpass that this year.
And it isn’t just SickKids or Canada. A survey published by the Canadian Pediatric Society (CPS) conducted from late 2025 to early 2026 details various e-scooter crashes, including 26 hospitalizations lasting over two days, 12 intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and 10 deaths. Head injuries were present in about half the cases.
Moreover, most of the severe injury cases involve riders who didn’t wear helmets, and most involved boys aged between 10 and 15 years old. So, obviously, wear a helmet and use proper protection when riding e-scooters, but there’s more to it than that.
Part of the issue stems from unclear regulations around e-scooters. They’re often marketed as toys, but can reach high speeds, sometimes going from zero to 40km/h in a matter of seconds. In some cases, top speeds can reach as fast as 70km/h. Couple those high speeds with young riders who might not be familiar with the rules of the road and who are typically less risk-averse, and it’s a recipe for severe injuries.
Canada does have some rules in place around e-scooters, but the laws can vary significantly from province to province. Some provinces, including Ontario, Quebec, and B.C., cap e-scooter speeds around 25km/h. Other provinces and some cities have banned the devices entirely.
Clearer rules around e-scooters could help improve safety, whether that’s improving issues around batteries or preventing more kids from injuring themselves riding scooters. It’s just a matter of figuring out what those rules should be.

articles.title: Google announces Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after previous release
articles.text:
Google is announcing a new Gemini model today, but it’s not the long-awaited 3.5 Pro. Gemini 3.7 Flash is now rolling out to replace 3.6 Flash, which itself was released only three weeks ago. This new “workhorse” model is supposedly the product of core optimizations and developer feedback, offering improved coding and agentic performance. And Google is hoping to counter the lower cost of some competing models with a lower “introductory price” for 3.7 Flash.
According to Senior Director Tulsee Doshi, Gemini 3.7 Flash is noticeably better at coding than the previous Flash release. She cites a jump in the FrontierCode 1.1 Main test from 34.4 to 43.6 percent and DeepSWE v1.1 going from 49 to 65.3 percent. As for the vibes, Gemini 3.7 Flash’s WebDev Arena score has risen to 1,588 from 1,538.
People turning to Gemini and hoping it will “know” things may also see modest improvements in Gemini 3.7 Flash. The GDP.pdf benchmark, which measures how well a model can process complex documents, has gone up to 34 percent versus 22 percent with 3.6 Flash. AutomationBench tests how well models can execute common business workflows, and Gemini 3.7 Flash rose to 30.4 percent from 3.6’s 17 percent score.
Those numbers certainly are higher. But are they sufficiently different to support a new model release just three weeks after the last one? This may be more about maintaining the appearance of constant improvements in Google’s AI. Throughout 2024 and 2025, Google rapidly made up ground to rival the best AI coming out of competing AI labs. Things appear to have slowed in 2026, though. At I/O in May, Google promised that the flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro would launch in June, but that never happened.

articles.title: Twitch choque avec son IA qui s'entraîne sur les streamers : « Si c’était optionnel, personne ne l’activerait »
articles.text:
Twitch entraînera l'IA générative d'Amazon sur les contenus de ses streamers, par défaut. Son patron produit justifie le choix avec une franchise rare : demander la permission reviendrait à ne jamais l'obtenir. Les créateurs apprécieront.
Il y a des aveux qui valent tous les communiqués de presse. Lors de son émission « Patch Notes » diffusée le 12 août, et relayée notamment par TechCrunch, Twitch a annoncé que les diffusions de ses streamers alimenteraient désormais l'entraînement des modèles d'IA générative d'Amazon, sa maison mère depuis 2014. L'option est activée d'office, et c'est Mike Minton, directeur produit de la plateforme, qui en a résumé la philosophie en direct : « Si c'était optionnel, personne ne l'activerait. Honnêtement, c'est la réponse. »
Une case cochée d'avance, à vous de la trouver
Devant environ 3 000 spectateurs (un chiffre modeste pour une annonce de cette ampleur, mais Internet s'est chargé de la caisse de résonance), Mike Minton a détaillé un dispositif dont la mécanique tient en une phrase. Les contenus diffusés sur les chaînes serviront de matière première aux modèles d'Amazon, sauf opposition explicite du créateur. La manœuvre rappelle ces assurances voyage pré-cochées au fond des tunnels d'achat en ligne : rien n'est caché, tout est simplement rangé là où personne ne regarde.
- Tri et filtrage efficaces des vidéos répertoriées sur la plateforme.
- Fonctionnalités de monétisation accessibles à tous les porte-monnaies.
- Interface réactive et agréable sur le web comme sur l'app mobile.
Le bouton existe bel et bien, mais il ne loge pas dans le tableau de bord créateur que les streamers ouvrent chaque jour. Il faut passer par les paramètres de la chaîne, puis par l'onglet dédié à la sécurité et à la confidentialité, pour y trouver l'option d'entraînement des IA génératives et la désactiver. Le dirigeant assume l'arbitrage sans détour, expliquant en substance que le consentement volontaire aurait condamné le projet. On saluera au moins la sincérité, denrée rare dans un secteur qui préfère d'ordinaire les périphrases sur « l'amélioration de l'expérience utilisateur ».
Ce que le droit européen a déjà dit du procédé
Ce mécanisme d'opposition a posteriori, l'Europe le connaît par cœur. Meta a ouvert la voie le 27 mai 2025 en lançant l'entraînement de ses modèles sur les contenus publics de Facebook et Instagram, sur la base juridique de l'intérêt légitime plutôt que du consentement. La méthode a survécu à sa première épreuve judiciaire, un tribunal allemand ayant refusé de la bloquer en mai 2025. Elle reste toutefois contestée par les associations de défense de la vie privée dans plusieurs pays de l'Union. Google a suivi le mouvement avec une collecte par défaut pour entraîner Gemini, preuve que l'opt-out est devenu le réglage d'usine de toute l'industrie.
Côté français, la CNIL a publié en juin 2025 ses fiches sur l'intérêt légitime appliqué au développement de l'IA : la base légale est admise, à condition d'offrir une information claire et un droit d'opposition effectif. Autrement dit, la légalité du dispositif de Twitch se jouera moins sur le principe que sur l'accessibilité réelle du fameux bouton (celui rangé deux menus plus loin, donc). Et le dossier comporte une seconde couche, car les streamers ne sont pas de simples utilisateurs mais des auteurs. Leur contenu convoque donc aussi le règlement européen sur l'IA et le droit d'opposition prévu par la directive droit d'auteur de 2019. Avec une audience française qui se compterait en millions d'utilisateurs mensuels, le sujet dépasse largement le cercle des créateurs professionnels, comme le montre déjà la mobilisation autour des formulaires d'opposition de WhatsApp.
Pour les streamers français, refuser tient donc en trois clics dans les paramètres de chaîne ; pour Twitch, tout le pari repose sur le fait que la majorité ne les fera jamais.

articles.title: OpenAI lance Computer History sur Mac, une fonction qui enregistre l'activité entière de votre ordinateur
articles.text:
Et si ChatGPT se souvenait de tout ce que vous faites sur votre ordinateur, même en dehors de ChatGPT ?
Le 13 août 2026, OpenAI a annoncé le déploiement de Computer History dans son application de bureau sur macOS. Le principe : l’application observe ce que vous faites dans les applications et sur les sites que vous autorisez, en fait des résumés, et se sert de ces résumés comme contexte dans vos prochaines conversations avec ChatGPT et Codex. « ChatGPT peut désormais se souvenir de votre activité dans les applications et sur les sites web de votre ordinateur », résume l’entreprise sur X.
C’est quoi Computer History, la nouvelle mémoire de ChatGPT ?
Jusqu’ici, la mémoire de ChatGPT se limitait à ce que vous lui aviez dit dans ChatGPT. Computer History élargit le périmètre à l’ensemble de votre activité informatique : le navigateur, l’éditeur de texte, vos messageries perso et pro (Slack, Teams), le terminal, l’application de notes, etc.
L’application construit une frise chronologique de votre journée, découpée par blocs de quelques minutes. Chaque entrée contient un titre, un résumé en texte de ce que vous avez fait, et la liste des applications qui ont contribué à ce résumé. Exemple donné par OpenAI dans sa documentation : « Vous avez relu le plan de lancement, vérifié l’implémentation et récupéré des retours avant de mettre à jour la documentation. »
Ces résumés deviennent ensuite du contexte réutilisable. OpenAI met en avant trois usages :
- Reprendre où vous en étiez : « sur quoi je travaillais avant ma pause ? », sans avoir à réexpliquer les fichiers ouverts et les étapes suivantes.
- Retrouver un document : « où est la proposition que je consultais ce matin ? ». ChatGPT se sert de la frise pour identifier la source, puis va la lire directement.
- Automatiser une routine : quand le système repère une tâche répétitive, il propose de la transformer en « skill » ou en automatisation, par exemple un récapitulatif quotidien de votre travail.
Sur certains aspects, Computer History rappelle ce qu’Apple veut faire avec Siri AI… sauf que son système repose sur un index sémantique purement local avec moins de compréhension de tout ce qu’il se passe.
Computer History ne fait pas de captures d’écran… mais interroge sur la vie privée
Conscient des enjeux de vie privée, OpenAI explique que Computer History enregistre des « événements d’interaction » exposés par le système d’accessibilité de macOS : les clics, la saisie au clavier, les raccourcis, les changements d’application et le contexte que macOS rend disponible. Aucune capture d’écran n’est jamais enregistrée sans votre accord.
« Computer History ne repose pas sur la capture d’écran ou audio. À la place, il capture des événements d’interaction comme les clics, la frappe, les changements d’application et plus encore, ce qui lui permet de créer des mémoires plus vite et plus efficacement. », explique Dominik Kundel, d’OpenAI, dans la vidéo d’annonce. L’application ne demande d’ailleurs pas l’autorisation d’enregistrement de l’écran de macOS :
- Les événements sont capturés localement sur le Mac, dans un espace isolé (l’App Group de ChatGPT), et supprimés au bout de 48 heures.
- Périodiquement, une session Codex éphémère résume ces événements. Ce traitement a lieu sur les serveurs d’OpenAI, qui indique ne pas conserver les fichiers d’événements après traitement, sauf obligation légale, et ne pas s’en servir pour entraîner ses modèles.
- Les mémoires générées sont ensuite stockées en local, sous forme de fichiers Markdown lisibles et modifiables, dans le dossier des mémoires de Codex.
Reste une réalité : ChatGPT se construit un historique de votre vie numérique sans que vous le sollicitiez. Il va largement plus loin que dans sa mémoire précédente… avec le risque de se faire piéger par des injections de prompt cachées dans des sites web. Pour rassurer, OpenAI indique que l’on peut choisir les applications surveillées, que la navigation privée n’est jamais enregistrée et qu’une icône dans la barre de menus indique quand il y a un enregistrement.
Une disponibilité réservée aux abonnés Pro… sauf en Europe
Computer History est réservé à l’application de bureau ChatGPT sur macOS, pour les abonnés Pro, Business et Enterprise. Il n’y a rien pour les comptes gratuits ni pour les abonnés Plus à ce stade.
En France, il faudra patienter. La documentation d’OpenAI indique que Computer History n’est pas disponible dans l’Espace économique européen, en Suisse et au Royaume-Uni. Plusieurs médias américains évoquent un déploiement dans ces zones « dans les prochaines semaines », sans calendrier précis. Reste à déterminer si la fonction est facile à mettre en conformité avec les règlements européens.

articles.title: Au moment d'annoncer les Pixel 11, Google baisse discrètement les prix des Pixel 10
articles.text:
Google profite de l’été pour renouveler sa gamme de smartphones. Les Pixel 11 débarquent au nombre de quatre sur le marché avec des évolutions somme toute mineures, même si cela reste toujours bon à prendre pour l’utilisateur. Si le géant américain limite la flambée tarifaire, c’est bien ses prédécesseurs qui risquent d’en profiter dans les prochains jours. En effet, Google n’a pas abandonné la série Pixel 10 et a discrètement revu sa grille tarifaire à la baisse pour écouler ses derniers modèles de l’année dernière.
Des baisses de prix officielles avant la rupture de stock
Sur la boutique officielle de la marque, le ticket d’entrée a clairement été revu à la baisse. Le Pixel 10 classique est passé de 899 à 799 euros, et le Pixel 10 Pro affiche désormais 999 euros au lieu des 1 099 euros demandés jusqu’ici.
Mieux vaut toutefois ne pas trop tarder si ces modèles vous intéressent : plusieurs versions sont déjà en rupture de stock. Notons au passage que certains modèles, comme le Pixel 10 Pro XL ou le Pixel 10 Pro Fold, ne bénéficient pas de cette baisse.
Une décote encore plus forte chez les autres revendeurs
Si l’offre officielle du constructeur est déjà alléchante, il est possible de faire encore mieux en fouinant un peu en dehors des sentiers battus. De nombreux revendeurs tiers cherchent eux aussi à faire de la place dans leurs rayons pour accueillir la onzième itération de la gamme.
En surveillant attentivement les grandes enseignes de e-commerce, on peut facilement dénicher ces mêmes Pixel 10 à des prix encore plus agressifs. Cette dynamique commerciale creuse un écart tarifaire absolument massif avec les modèles fraîchement annoncés, rendant le rapport qualité-prix de la génération 10 pratiquement imbattable sur le segment haut de gamme.
Le choix de la raison technologique
Les Pixel 11 ne sont pas dénués d’intérêt pour autant. Le capteur principal passe à 48 Mpx, la puce Tensor G6 promet des gains de puissance notables, et le Pixel 11 Pro innove avec son module « Hilight » à l’arrière ou sa dictée vocale améliorée Rambler.
Toutefois, pour qui n’a pas besoin de la toute dernière nouveauté, l’écart avec le Pixel 10 s’annonce ténu au quotidien : celui-ci demeure solide en photographie, profite de la plupart des avancées côté intelligence artificielle, et surtout bénéficie de la promesse de Google d’assurer sept années de mises à jour logicielles. De quoi faire du Pixel 10 une alternative raisonnable, pour qui préfère l’expérience Android pure sans payer le prix fort.

articles.title: Life after Chandra: Could a Next-Gen Tata be groomed for the top job?
articles.text:
Life after Chandra: Could a next-gen Tata be groomed for the top job?
Who could lead Tata Group after N Chandrasekaran? Explore the succession race and whether Leah, Maya or Neville Tata could emerge as future leaders.
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust said today that its trustees have passed a resolution to initiate the setting up of a Selection Committee, formally opening the Tata Sons chairman succession process.
The move follows N Chandrasekaran conveying to the trust's nominee directors that he would not offer himself for re-appointment when his current tenure expires on 20 February 2027.
In its statement, the trust said it respected the decision and placed on record its deepest appreciation for his contribution and stewardship of Tata Sons and the Tata Group over the past decade. It added that it would extend full support to Tata Sons in ensuring a smooth, timely and orderly transition of leadership.
Chandrasekaran wrote to the nominee directors on 12 August 2026. He has not resigned. Lawyers have pointed out that he has only stated he will not be available for re-appointment in February 2027. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust is the largest single shareholder in Tata Sons with close to 28%, while the Sir Ratan Tata Trust holds 24%.
While the immediate focus will be on who succeeds Chandrasekaran, the transition also raises a longer-term question for the group: could one of Noel Tata's three children, Leah, Maya or Neville, be groomed for an eventual leadership role at Tata Sons?
How the Tata Sons chairman succession will be decided
The process is governed by Article 118 of the Tata Sons Articles of Association, which requires a Selection Committee as long as the Tata Trusts together hold at least 40% of the paid-up ordinary share capital. The committee has five members: three jointly nominated by the two main trusts, one from the Tata Sons board and one independent external member chosen by the board.
The two trusts also pick the committee's chairperson from among their three nominees, and the committee only recommends a candidate. The formal appointment is made by the Tata Sons board under Article 121.
The same mechanism produced Chandrasekaran in January 2017, after a five-member panel unanimously recommended the then TCS chief executive. Unlike the disorderly transition of 2016, Tata Sons has roughly seven months this time.
The names already in circulation
Tata Steel's T V Narendran has emerged as one of the frontrunners, with Tata Sons chief financial officer Saurabh Agrawal and Tata Motors managing director and chief executive Shailesh Chandra also named by people familiar with the matter. Reports also place TCS chief K Krithivasan and Tata Chemicals veteran R Mukundan in the wider pool.
Group convention, under which executives retire from operational roles at 65 and non-executive directors at 70, could work against several of them, though it is an internal norm rather than a legal requirement and the board can waive it.
Narendran and Mukundan, in particular, represent the kind of long-serving Tata insiders who could provide continuity at the top while the group thinks about succession over a much longer horizon.
Whether a Tata returns to the top table
That is what makes the family question interesting. Noel Tata chairs the Tata Trusts and sits on the Tata Sons board as their nominee, but he is not chairman of Tata Sons. He is due to retire as vice-chairman of Titan in November 2026 on reaching 70, under the group's own retirement policy.
His three children are already inside the structure. Leah Tata leads the Taj hotel business, Neville Tata heads Trent's hypermarket chain Star Bazaar, and all three serve on the boards of smaller entities within Tata Trusts, with Neville additionally on the board of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust. Maya Tata, who worked at Tata Capital and then Tata Digital, is reported to be taking charge of Westside's digital expansion at Trent.
The three also became direct Tata Sons shareholders in 2026 after inheriting two shares each from their grandmother Simone Tata. The group has a template for grooming a successor in plain sight. Cyrus Mistry was appointed deputy chairman in November 2011 and succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman only in December 2012.
Any move to position the next generation would more plausibly follow that route than a direct elevation. Among the three, Neville's position within the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust gives him the most direct exposure to the ownership structure, while Leah has spent the longest period in an operating Tata company and Maya has worked across finance, digital and retail.
How their responsibilities evolve after the latest transition could therefore be as significant as the choice of the next chairman itself.
Why Noel Tata cannot simply take the Tata Sons chair
Noel Tata's name will inevitably surface in any discussion about bringing a Tata family member back to the top. But age is only one part of the equation. It is the group's own governance architecture that presents a bigger hurdle.
Ratan Tata was the last person to hold dual roles as chairman of Tata Trusts and chairman emeritus of Tata Sons, and in 2022 Tata Sons amended its Articles of Association to prevent one individual from holding both. Because Noel Tata currently chairs the Tata Trusts, that provision stands between him and the Tata Sons chair.
Even if the group's retirement conventions were relaxed, Noel would therefore need to give up the Trusts chairmanship or Tata Sons would have to revisit the separation of the two roles. Reversing it would mean the trusts effectively rewriting the separation between ownership and management that the group put in place after the Mistry dispute. That is a far larger decision than a personnel one.
The committee now has to move quickly. Whoever it recommends inherits the expansion of Air India, a semiconductor project and the task of remaking Tata Consultancy Services for an AI-driven market. Reports indicate Tata Group stocks have already taken a single-day hit of about Rs 47,412 crore since the announcement, which sharpens the pressure to name a successor well before February 2027 rather than at the wire.
For now, the immediate race is likely to be among experienced Tata executives such as Narendran, Mukundan and other senior group leaders. But the more consequential succession story could play out one level below: whether the group starts preparing Leah, Maya or Neville Tata for a much bigger role in the years ahead.
Edited by Adith Charlie

articles.title: Data analyst sent to prison for stealing data, extorting employer
articles.text:
A former data analyst contractor for Brightly Software has been sentenced to two years in prison for targeting his employer in a $2.5 million extortion scheme.
Brightly is a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) company formerly known as SchoolDude, which was acquired by Siemens in August 2022. Brightly employs over 700 people and provides asset management and maintenance software to more than 12,000 clients worldwide.
27-year-old North Carolina man Cameron Curry (also known as "Loot") was found guilty in March of orchestrating an "extensive cyber extortion scheme" targeting his employer.
According to court documents, Curry stole sensitive documents after gaining access to the company's payroll information and corporate data, which he later used to extort Brightly after learning that his six-month contract wouldn't be extended.
One day after his contract ended on December 10, he emailed dozens of Brightly employees using the Loot alias and the lootsoftware@outlook.com email address between December 11, 2023, and January 24, 2024, threatening to leak the stolen information unless he was paid a $2.5 million ransom in cryptocurrency.
"We will commence the process of disseminating salary information starting January 1, 2024 in phases to all employees and will report you to the SEC after for not reporting the breach," Curry said in one of the extortion messages.
"If you wish to reclaim your data, we recommend doing so promptly at 2.5 million USD in order to save your company and stocks, as each subsequent month will incur a $100,000 USD increase. Discrepancies in your books are currently over 16 million USD, posing a potential risk for retention issues, a hostile work environment, resentment, and more."
He also attached screenshots of employees' personally identifiable information (PII), including their names, dates of birth, home addresses, and compensation information, and threatened to report Brightly to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for failing to disclose the breach.
Following Curry's many extortion emails, Brightly paid $7,540 in Bitcoin, transferring the funds to a cryptocurrency wallet controlled by Curry.
After the company reported the incident to law enforcement, the FBI searched Curry's residence on January 24 and seized various electronic devices containing evidence that linked him to the extortion scheme.
"We are aware of the U.S. Department of Justice's (DOJ) convictions of Cameron Curry for extortion," Brightly told BleepingComputer in March.
"We have fully cooperated with the FBI and DOJ in this matter and appreciate their investigative efforts. Given that these proceedings are pending, we defer all questions to law enforcement authorities."
In May 2023, Brightly also disclosed a data breach (unrelated to this case) after attackers stole credentials and personal data (including names, email addresses, account passwords, phone numbers) of nearly 3 million customers and users from the database of its SchoolDude online platform.

articles.title: Nigeria wants to tax crypto. Traders say it could slow business.
articles.text: Peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency traders and over-the-counter (OTC) dealers say Nigeria’s new virtual asset tax framework —which mandates a 1.5% stamp duty charge on digital assets—risks raising trading costs and potentially driving activity away from regulated exchanges and into less visible channels. Joshua Adedeji, a Nigerian OTC bulk trader who said he processes about $500,000 worth of USDT—a dollar-backed stablecoin—weekly on cryptocurrency exchange Bybit , said the tax cost is far higher than his existing operating costs. “Transfer charges were my biggest transaction costs before,” Adedeji said. “Now, stamp duty and other taxes [will account for] much higher costs, because the higher percentage of the tax is on transactions.” The compliance burden will weigh heavily on crypto traders who rely on very small price differences to make money. Frequent stamp duty deductions increase the cost of moving money between wallets, exchanges, and customers, cutting into already thin margins for day traders and swing traders who buy and sell cryptocurrencies to speculate on price movements. Adedeji said he typically earns about ₦0.5 ($0.00037) per USDT on spreads when trading cryptocurrencies. He processes transactions for over 100 customers weekly, according to him. “The heart of P2P is the volume of transactions, which doesn’t necessarily translate into profit,” he said. “Taxing multiple points of transactions will definitely have a bad ripple effect on P2P.” He expects trading volumes to fall sharply if the tax rules are enforced strictly. “Volume of P2P will reduce drastically, because the margins of profit are slim, before even factoring in losses,” Adedeji said. Kenny Olawale, a Lagos-based crypto trader who trades P2P on the agent-based stablecoin startup, Accrue , said he expects to see a similar squeeze. He said his business processes between $2,000 and $10,000 weekly across 50–150 customers, and that stablecoin adoption among non-crypto-native users has been rising in recent months. Before the new rules, his major business costs were bank transfer charges, including existing stamp duties for fiat bank transfers —₦50 ($0.037) for transactions above ₦10,000 ($7.34)—and blockchain network fees, according to him. He said the 1.5% crypto stamp duty could become problematic for stablecoins used for cross-border payments and daily expenditure. “The turnaround for exchanges when one user is funding a virtual card and another is paying at a restaurant doesn’t even count as investment with a big return,” Olawale said. “Charging 1.5% on each leg makes it all ridiculous.” He said P2P spreads have narrowed to as little as ₦2–₦5 per dollar, leaving little room to absorb additional taxes. “I think [the tax rules] will be bad for the ecosystem and adoption of stablecoins for easy payment settlement,” Olawale said. “Users generally don’t like to pay for spending their own money again. When the dust settles, we might need to stop trading or reduce it significantly to limit losses.” Taxing the breadth of Nigeria’s virtual asset economy Nigeria’s new tax guidelines, signed on July 31 and announced by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) on August 3, introduce a 1.5% stamp duty on virtual asset transfers, including cryptocurrencies and stablecoins. They also require exchanges to deduct withholding tax when users dispose of crypto assets, while a 7.5% value-added tax (VAT) applies to taxable services and transaction fees charged by virtual asset service providers (VASPs). The framework goes beyond retail trading. Virtual asset companies will also pay VAT fees on almost every transaction that counts as a source of revenue, such as brokerage commissions, withdrawal and transaction fees, and listing fees paid by token issuers seeking to have their assets listed on exchanges. Crypto companies operating in Nigeria are also subject to 30% company income tax, as Nigeria seeks to drive up collections. Traders say the combined effect is that taxes would apply at multiple stages of a transaction: when money enters the crypto system, when assets are transferred, and when they are sold. P2P traders who buy and sell digital assets through centralised exchanges such as Bybit, Bitget, and Binance P2P—or through informal channels such as WhatsApp and Telegram—will not be spared. Under the guidelines, centralised P2P platforms that hold buyers’ funds in escrow until a trade is completed would be responsible for deducting applicable taxes before releasing funds. Platforms that merely provide a marketplace without taking custody of customer funds must keep records and report transactions to the NRS. Individual P2P traders and OTC dealers handling large volumes of crypto liquidity are expected to declare and remit applicable taxes directly to the authorities, with penalties for non-compliance. Questions over enforcement Industry operators say the framework differs from most major jurisdictions, such as the United Kingdom, where tax is typically triggered by a realised gain—the profit made when an asset is sold for more than its purchase price. Kenya proposed a 10% excise duty on the transaction fees that VASPs charge. Opeyemi Akinremi, co-founder of B2B crypto payments startup Ivorypay and consumer-facing exchange Duffle , said Nigeria’s framework taxes the entire transaction lifecycle. “Tax becomes payable even when there’s no profit at all, eroding capital regardless of outcome,” Akinremi said. He illustrated the effect with a hypothetical ₦1 million ($734) Bitcoin purchase. A 1.5% stamp duty would deduct ₦15,000 ($11) on entry. Selling the asset the next day at the same price could trigger about ₦9,850 ($7.23) in withholding tax, costing the trader ₦24,850 ($18.25) in taxes—excluding exchange fees—despite recording no gain. “A trader who loses money on a bad call would still pay entry and exit tax on top of that loss, because the tax is triggered by the transaction itself, not by whether any economic gain occurred,” Akinremi said. He said the government’s approach is to enforce collectability by turning cryptocurrency exchanges and other VASPs into withholding agents, ensuring revenue is captured before funds leave the regulated system. However, he warned that the framework could create a strong incentive for traders to migrate to P2P channels, OTC desks and offshore platforms that have no obligation to deduct or remit Nigerian taxes. “Once going through a regulated Nigerian exchange starts costing you 2.5%–3% per trade, a rational trader starts asking why they would do this on a platform that taxes them when they can do the same trade elsewhere and keep that money,” he said. Yet, when it comes to offshore crypto trading, Nigeria’s tax authority is making that responsibility lie solely on the user. When retail users buy and sell virtual assets on foreign exchanges, they must declare all applicable taxes, according to the guidelines. Despite the broad collection obligations, the mechanism for deducting and remitting the taxes remains unclear , Akinremi said. “The obligation is clear, but the mechanism isn’t,” he said. “Withholding tax, stamp duty, and VAT are defined, but there’s no mature government portal or API [application programming interface] to remit through, so VASPs have to build that infrastructure themselves.” The compliance burden is compounded by the complexity of cryptocurrency markets, where multiple blockchains, token types, and external wallets interact in ways traditional financial systems do not. “The question is not whether crypto should be taxed—it should,” Akinremi said. “The question is whether the tax structure encourages users and businesses to operate transparently within Nigeria or unintentionally encourages migration to less visible markets.” Fear of driving activity underground Rume Ophi, programmes and communications lead at the Virtual Asset Service Provider Association (VASPA), an industry advocacy group, believes crypto taxation is inevitable and welcomed the government’s recognition of crypto as part of Nigeria’s financial system. However, he noted that imposing heavy transaction taxes too early in the formalisation process could undermine compliance efforts. “When you start a tax regime for an industry that has gone through all sorts of harassment, you create another opportunity for people to bypass compliance,” Ophi said. He called for a review of the framework and suggested temporary tax reliefs or thresholds for startups and smaller market participants to encourage growth before imposing broad transaction levies. Olayimika Oyebanji, legal consultant to the House of Representatives Ad-Hoc Committee on the Economic, Regulatory and Security Implications of Cryptocurrency Adoption and PoS Operations, described the framework as “a global anomaly.” “Tax obligations are often triggered at the point of realisation due to the convertible nature of virtual assets,” Oyebanji said. “However, taxing every stage of a virtual asset transaction [in Nigeria’s case] violates the tax canon of fairness.” Nigeria, he added, already operates a dual crypto market: a formal exchange-driven sector and a much larger informal P2P network that conducts significant trading through WhatsApp groups, Telegram channels, OTC desks, and other unregulated channels. “This framework will not reduce overall trading activity,” Oyebanji said. “There is a strong likelihood that trading activities will remain in the shadows, far beyond the reach and visibility of the taxman.” Stronger record-keeping, reporting obligations, and tax collection processes could help legitimise the sector. However, operators say layering transaction taxes on top of profit taxes risks weakening liquidity on domestic exchanges and stalling stablecoin adoption. “Formalising VASPs—[introducing] Tax IDs, record-keeping, and reporting obligations—is reasonable and overdue,” Akinremi said. “Where the policy overreaches is layering an entry-and-exit transaction tax on top of the gains tax. A framework built for government revenue certainty ends up undermining its own revenue base by taxing the act of trading itself.” For traders such as Adedeji and Olawale, the tension dances around whether running a P2P business can remain a profitable venture once every virtual asset transfer, conversion, and sale is taxed. True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: El misterioso "punto rojo" que vimos en el eclipse de ayer tiene nombre y apellidos: así explica la ciencia este fascinante fenómeno
articles.text:
En el día de ayer, buena parte de España salió a la calle para mirar al cielo y disfrutar del eclipse solar total que nos regaló minutos de oscuridad en pleno día y dejó imágenes para la historia. Sin embargo, más allá del espectacular anillo de luz y la corona solar, hubo un detalle que sorprendió a muchas personas, que fue un punto rojo pero intenso que asomaba justo por el borde de la silueta de la Luna.
Llamaradas asomando en la oscuridad. Para entender qué fue exactamente lo que vimos, debemos recurrir a la anatomía del Sol. Tal y como explicó el conocido meteorólogo Roberto Brasero, esos misteriosos puntos rojos que aparecían alrededor de la Luna durante la fase de totalidad son, en realidad, fulguraciones o protuberancias solares. Se trata de gigantescas "llamaradas" que emergen de la superficie del Sol y que, en nuestro día a día, resultan completamente invisibles debido al brillo cegador de la estrella.
Pero cuando la Luna actúa como un escudo perfecto y oculta la fotosfera del Sol, de repente permite que veamos las capas superiores de la atmósfera de nuestra estrella. Y eso precisamente ha sido caldo de cultivo para las numerosas investigaciones que se llevaron a cabo en la noche de ayer.
Lo que es. Tanto la NASA como la Agencia Espacial Europea han estudiado y documentado este fenómeno a fondo en eclipses anteriores. La ciencia nos dice que ese punto rojo es, con una altísima probabilidad, una protuberancia solar.
Esto no es más que una inmensa concentración de plasma de la cromosfera que se mantiene suspendida sobre la superficie del Sol gracias a sus potentísimos y complejos campos magnéticos, como ha explicado Frontera Espacial en su cuenta de X.
Su color no es una casualidad, y la ESA explica que la emisión roja más intensa que vemos en esa capa procede del hidrógeno. En términos astrofísicos, este tono rojizo es el resultado directo de la emisión del gas, concretamente en lo que se conoce como la línea H-alfa. Esta línea de emisión se sitúa exactamente en una longitud de onda de 656,3 nanómetros y, al quedar bloqueada la luz blanca de la fotosfera, nuestros ojos por fin son capaces de captar esta particular luz rojiza que el Sol emite constantemente.
No hay que confundirse. Durante los segundos mágicos que preceden o siguen a la totalidad, el borde lunar se convierte en un festival de fenómenos ópticos y físicos. El material educativo de la NASA es muy claro a la hora de diferenciar las estructuras brillantes que sobresalen del borde solar.
Por ejemplo, el halo alrededor de casi todo el borde de la luna es la cromosfera en sí misma. Es la capa de la atmósfera solar situada justo por encima de la fotosfera. Suele dejarse ver como un anillo rojizo durante unos breves segundos justo al inicio y al final de la totalidad. Además, también se puede ver un punto blanco muy brillante, conocido como el 'anillo de diamantes' que son las llamadas Perlas de Baily, que se trata de los últimos rayos de luz blanca de la fotosfera que consiguieron colarse a través de los escarpados valles, cráteres y montañas del relieve de la propia Luna.

articles.title: Fuite des impôts : les données de presque 700 000 personnes dans la nature (revenus fiscaux, taux d’imposition, adresse…)
articles.text:
Fuite des impôts : les données de presque 700 000 personnes dans la nature (revenus fiscaux, taux d’imposition, adresse…)
Les données fiscales de plus de 600 000 contribuables sont désormais en vente, suite à une intrusion datant de juin dernier au sein des services des impôts. Gare aux arnaques dans les semaines à venir.
Il ne fait toujours pas bon d’être français, avec des fuites de données à tire-larigot. La dernière en date concerne la DGFiP, alias le fisc pour les intimes, qui aurait laissé sortir les données d’exactement 678 437 personnes. Entre revenus fiscaux, adresses, échanges avec les impôts et taux d’imposition en vente sur le dark web, des campagnes de phishing bien ficelées se profilent à l’horizon.
Ça fuite encore dans le service des impôts, les Français victimes jusqu’aux revenus fiscaux
Révélée par FrenchBreaches ce 13 août 2026, cette cyberattaque des impôts proviendrait d’une intrusion survenue en juin 2026. Le pirate ayant mis en vente cette base de données prétend avoir infiltré des serveurs internes pour obtenir un accès VPN, qui lui aurait ensuite permis d’utiliser un outil interne pour extraire massivement ces données.
L’exfiltration aurait été rapidement interrompue après sa détection, mais le mal est fait : un fichier regroupant toutes les données collectées est déjà en vente pour plusieurs milliers d’euros sur le dark web. Dans les détails, 392 867 dossiers concerneraient les particuliers, contre 285 570 pour les professionnels.
Au-delà des coordonnées (nom, prénom, date et lieu de naissance, situation familiale, adresse postale et mail ou encore numéro de téléphone), les informations compromises dressent un profil d’une précision redoutable. On y trouve en effet :
- L’identifiant fiscal
- Le revenu fiscal de référence
- Le taux de prélèvement à la source
- Le nombre de parts fiscales et de personnes à charge
- Les informations relatives au conjoint
- L’historique des échanges avec l’administration.
Dans une mise à jour datant de ce matin 7 h, FrenchBreaches ajoute que 26 805 des comptes récupérés auraient un revenu fiscal de référence de 100 000 € ou plus, 386 dépasseraient 1 million d’euros et 8 dépasseraient 10 millions d’euros. Un niveau de détail qui fait froid dans le dos, et surtout qui ouvre incontestablement la porte à des campagnes de phishing ciblées très dangereuses, avec beaucoup de données pouvant être utilisées pour tromper de futures victimes.
Comme toute fuite, elle doit encore être confirmée par la principale intéressée : la DGFiP. Pour l’instant, ce n’est pas le cas, ce qui laisse encore planer le doute sur sa véracité. À titre de rappel, la précédente fuite de fin janvier 2026 avait été confirmée environ deux semaines plus tard à la mi-février. Peut-être que ce sera aussi le cas cette fois-ci, ou que l’administration fiscale réfutera l’incident.
